#1922. Keith Wyness explains unexpected Man United 49 per cent boardroom increase

Manchester United fans shouldn't read too much into the fact that the value of shares in their club has climbed during 2026.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that United's ownership are not primarily focused on financial gain.

This comes after Kieran Maguire revealed that the price of United's shares has grown by 49 per cent since the start of 2026, despite the team's fortunes on the pitch.

However, Wyness believes that the increase may merely be down to less people selling their shares in the club, creating scarcity in the market.

United are currently languishing inside the relegation zone, and are arguably at one of the lowest ebbs in their lengthy history.

Expectations would suggest that should coincide with the club's valuation on the stock market dropping, but Wyness outlined why that is not always the case.

Manchester United share price is up 49% in 2026. Perhaps that is where the priorities of INEOS and co lie? https://t.co/ZAZW1UpmQr

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that the change in United's shares may be down to a natural "float."

He explained that floats are events that can dramatically change the price of shares, far more than usually expected.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained why fans shouldn't draw conclusions from the notable increase.

"You would think so from the outside looking at that, but the reality is there's a very small, what they call a float for these shares," he said.

"So events can make dramatic increases or decreases more than a normal share might do. So I wouldn't read too much into it.

"It's just the fact that very few shares being traded can lead to different price increases. I don't see the share price being a great indicator of United's position right now."

Wyness previously told Football Insider last week that the latest "noises" from Old Trafford suggest that Bruno Fernandes will still sign a new contract.

The club captain recently rejected a second offer of a new deal from the Red Devils, as his long-term future remains hugely uncertain.

However, Wyness believes that new manager Mauricio Pochettino will be capable of repairing the relationship with Fernandes in the coming months.

The Portuguese is out of contract at the end of the season, although United have the option of an additional one-year extension.

#1920. Keith Wyness suggests how far PIF are from agreeing £1.5bn Newcastle sale

Newcastle United's PIF ownership could potentially sell the club for £1.5billion once they establish their new training ground and planned new stadium.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the club is already worth as much as £900million.

Recent reports have suggested that an announcement over plans for a new stadium on Tyneside could be just around the corner, which would boost the valuation even further.

However, Wyness does not expect a sale to truly be on PIF's radar for another three to five years at least.

Newcastle are hoping to have their training ground ready for the 2029-30 campaign, and a change of stadium could closely follow.

PIF's future at the club has been up in the air of late, but Wyness still believes they will at least see those projects through before pulling away.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that PIF simply wouldn't get the necessary rewards by selling the Magpies soon.

He outlined that they have already pumped around £600m into the club, so would have limited gain from a sale in the £900m ballpark.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained that a sale right now would have little benefit.

"Well, that's a difficult one because they paid £300m for the club and I think they've put in about £600m of their money so far. So you're already looking at £900m. Now that's just to get your money back," he said.

"You'd be looking at somewhere between £800m and £1bn would be the valuation I'd be looking at. However, if they were to put the training ground and stadium in place, then you could be looking at £1.2bn to £1.5bn in my opinion, depending on how the revenue and the size of the stadium pans out.

"That's the sort of time that they might consider a sale because they get some profit out of the whole thing. So I don't see it being any time soon; could be three to five years maybe.

"I don't really see a sale happening anytime soon because at present you wouldn't get the valuation they would need to make some money out of the whole thing."

Former Manchester City financial advisor Stefan Borson told Football Insider last weekend that Newcastle could potentially lose £75m a year on interest rates alone while building a new stadium.

The football finance expert noted that would be before the stage taking out a £1.5bn loan to help fund the project.

Borson pointed out that Newcastle will do well to secure an interest rate that is less than double the 2.5 per cent that Tottenham paid while building their new ground.

He pointed out that loan rates have climbed "even higher" since then, creating a difficult situation for Newcastle moving forward.

#1919. 'Scottish football has a serious problem, and Rangers are part of the reason' - ex-chief scout

Scottish football is facing a serious problem with developing talent to perform at the top level after the latest controversy at Rangers.

For the first time ever, there were no Scottish players named in either side's starting XI as Rangers beat Motherwell 2-1 in a close-fought clash at Fir Park on 21 November.

That has led to outrage from supporters and pundits, but underlines a bigger concern for Scottish football and the future for young talents coming through.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Rangers and other SPFL clubs are looking abroad in their efforts to improve their starting XIs.

Concerns have grown behind the scenes about the lack of top-class talents coming through in Scotland, and the lack of trust shown by their leading clubs in young players.

Sebastien Pogocnoli's national team side are also facing a decline given the low number of top emerging talents coming through, and something must be done to resolve it.

Brown told Football Insider during the summer that Rangers have to be clever with their recruitment, with scouts working across Europe to identify top young players.

While recruiting from within Scotland remains a big part of their plans, the increasing globalisation of the game means there are better deals to be had signing players from abroad.

Scottish players are being priced out of moves to top clubs, with Motherwell also part of the discussion, while clubs feel they cannot afford to take gambles.

"I think it's become clear that Scottish football has a serious problem at the moment," Brown told Football Insider.

"For there to be a game between two of the top Scottish clubs, Rangers and Motherwell, without a single Scottish player in either starting XI, that has got to be a worry.

"We've spoken before about the makeup of this Rangers squad and where they have to look to recruit players, and unfortunately, they're looking outside of Scotland.

"It can be pricey to sign domestic players, who come at a premium in every country, but at the same time, how many top young talents are coming through at the moment?

"There aren't any standout players in Scotland who you'd look at and think, Rangers have to go and sign him. That's the problem at the end of the day.

"These players aren't being produced at the moment, they're not coming through, and that's a problem not just for the clubs, but for the national team as well.

"It's hard to say what they can do about it, you can't force clubs to sign certain players if there aren't players of that top quality coming through.

"But it's certainly a concern and I'm sure discussions are being held about their next steps behind the scenes, because something has to be done to help the issue."

Rangers spend £35million to improve their squad during the summer, and will likely have to spend big again in January to address major weaknesses in Derek McInnes' side.

That is part of the problem in Scottish football, the top clubs are forced to look elsewhere to improve their squads if they wish to continue competing at the top level.

Football Insider revealed last month that Rangers are weighing up potential January transfers to improve their squad after assessing a number of key positions.

There are concerns that further injuries, which have been an issue this season, or unforeseen circumstances could mean Rangers are forced to act in the market.

There are also concerns about a number of players on the fringes of the squad, and potential departures or opportunities to upgrade are unlikely to be ignored.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1916. Crystal Palace 'will be relegated' if Thomas Frank does not make overhaul - ex-chief scout

Thomas Frank has inheirted a Crystal Palace side in freefall and must make major changes if he is to save them from relegation.

The boss got off to the worst possible start as his side suffered a late 3-2 defeat away at Coventry City, which once again exposed the weaknesses in their defence.

While Frank cannot be entirely blamed for the defeat, having had less than a week to train with his squad, it echoed the same issues that Palace have faced all season.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Frank has to make drastic changes if he is to turn Crystal Palace's miserable start to the season around.

The Eagles have now conceded the second-most goals of any club in Europe's top five league, second only to Man United, and leaked three again at the weekend.

That back line must immediately be addressed, whether that is with tactical tweaks on the pitch, a change of formation, or through recruitment in January.

Brown warned Football Insider on 17 November that Frank may have been set up to fail from the start at Crystal Palace after their failures in the transfer window.

The new boss has been presented with a squad which, particularly in defence, many beleive is not up to scratch for the level they are aiming to compete at.

Frank has praised his side's attacking profficiency, but that has never been an issue for Palace this season, and there are other areas which are in desperate need of attention.

"Crystal Palace are in a desperate situation and it's very hard to get out of it," Brown told Football Insider.

"For any club, when you're bottom of the table after this many games, it can feel impossible to turn things around no matter how well you play or how hard you work.

"If things continue the way they have been in defence, Crystal Palace will be relegated, and that shouldn't be a difficult thing to figure out.

"So Thomas Frank is going to have to make some major changes in that back line, he needs to figure out who his best players are, and maybe change the shape as well.

"It's not just a case of being a bit more organised or cutting out mistakes, because their problems are deeper than that, and the manager has got to do something about it.

"So like I say, a change of shape or extra work on the training ground, even bringing in new players in January, he has got to try everything to make them more solid.

"Because Palace are good going forward, they have plenty of goals in them and Frank has seen that, but if they keep leaking goals, there's no way they're going to start winning games."

Frank quickly emerged as the leading contender for the Crystal Palace job after Pierre Sage's dismissal, and the club hope he will be the man to reverse their fortunes.

Having sunk to the bottom of the Premier League table, the new boss is expected to turn things around, and they hope progress will be made in the coming weeks.

Football Insider revealed on 15 November that Frank's Premier League experience and remarkable work with Brentford made him the top choice.

The boss is also viewed as a good motivator, which is something Palace are searching for to improve their morale having dropped to the bottom of the Premier League table.

Crystal Palace hope Frank's reign will reflect the work he did with Brentford rather than with Tottenham, where he struggled, and believe he is the right man for the job.

#1915. Chelsea's dressing room 'know the writing is on the wall' for Xabi Alonso - expert

Chelsea are playing like a team who know that Xabi Alonso will soon be dismissed.

That is according to ex-manager and experienced former Tottenham, Aston Villa and Everton scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Blues were destroyed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, marking a first win for the away team in that fixture since 1999.

Alonso's team have won just one of their last five games across all competitions, and now find themselves 12 points off the top of the Premier League table.

The 44-year-old signed a four-year contract when he was appointed in the summer transfer window, but Chelsea have shown no hesitancy in making changes in the dugout before.

And with much of Stamford Bridge having voiced their disapproval on Saturday, the former Liverpool midfielder will now be under significant pressure to turn the situation around.

Chelsea seemed willing to try a new approach with the appointment of Alonso, signing more established, experienced players.

The likes of Jordan Henderson, Pep Chavarria and Danny Welbeck looked to be incomings directly approved by the Spaniard.

But it remains to be seen whether Chelsea are willing to take a different approach with how much patience they have for their manager, too.

Speaking to Football Insider, King said: "Alonso had a four-year deal at Real Madrid. How long did that last?

"I'm afraid Chelsea have shown in the past what they'll do. Look at the list of managers they've had. They will not hang about.

"And I don't think they show any patience at all. It's not fast food they're looking for, they're looking for fast results.

"One minute it looks as though he might be cracking it. The next minute [he doesn't]. It's what's on the pitch. It's what you put on the pitch.

"And for me, these players don't look as though they'll run through brick walls for him. It looks as though they know the writing is on the wall."

The home fans would have expected Chelsea to push forward when they went 1-0 up at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

But their lead lasted for just three minutes and they were ultimately lucky to only concede four. Alonso spoke of a lack of belief after the game, in hugely concerning quotes.

"After conceding we had to substitute [Moises] Caicedo and never recovered. Leeds believed more than us.

"We didn't show a good enough reaction. We need to find solutions together."

#1914. Romano: ‘The doors are open’ – Milan push to reunite Amorim with Sporting CP star Inacio

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that AC Milan are maintaining contacts with Goncalo Inacio’s entourage over a January move.

When Ruben Amorim arrived in the summer as the new head coach, Inacio was linked almost immediately. The pair know each other well as Amorim brought him into the side while at Sporting CP, making him a mainstay of the three-man defence.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Heading into January, Milan need reinforcements and especially at the back. Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori’s injuries have depleted the depth, which has led to Sankhoun Diawara being a starter perhaps a bit earlier than planned.

Earlier this week, Record in Portugal stated that Sporting are willing to part with Inacio in the winter window but only for the right price, which could be north of €40m. Still, it marks a step forward from the summer, when a late attempt failed.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano gave an update on Milan’s pursuit of a new central defender and he confirmed that Inacio seems to be the man in pole position.

“Let’s keep Gonçalo Inacio’s name there. Confirmation has also come from Portugal about what we’ve been telling you, that Inacio could be a key player in the January transfer window,” he said.

“I’m reiterating what I’ve been telling you for months, actually, about the relationships, because agent Miguel Pino is the same as Ruben Amorim’s agent. They’re all Portuguese, Amorim coached Inacio at Sporting. Arriving in January isn’t easy, though: it means being ready to be thrown into the fire.

“It’s not always easy. Signing Gonçalo Inacio would mean Amorim signing a player he knows, with whom he speaks the same language, not just verbally but also on the pitch. There’s a different feeling, he wouldn’t have to explain anything to the boy.

“Milan are keeping in touch with the player, his departure in January is possible, the doors are open if necessary. Then we need to understand the conditions, the prices, it’s clear that Sporting isn’t just interested in giving away a player like that for any price.

“They’ll have to negotiate, and last summer, Milan – amidst the ups and downs of this negotiation – at a certain point hoped to be able to secure a deal that could include a very expensive loan with an option to buy, to make everything easier from a financial standpoint. Milan have several names on the list, but Inacio’s is definitely one to consider.”

#1913. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

#1912. Ex-refs chief blasts Craig Pawson over Michael Kayode incident in Brentford vs Everton

Craig Pawson failed to act appropriately during Brentford's 4-0 victory against Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that the man in the middle relied too heavily on VAR as a "lifebelt".

Keane Lewis-Potter dragged a first-half brace, with Vitaly Janelt and Fabio Carvalho piling on the misery after the Toffees were sent down to 10 men.

Following a VAR review, James Tarkowski was given his marching orders for a studs-up challenge on Yehor Yarmoliuk in the 40th minute.

It was a very simple decision for Pawson after a second look at the incident, but fans were left wanting more from the official.

Just before the hour mark, Michael Kayode flew into a challenge on Jack Grealish, landing a big blow on the winger's shin, sparking angry calls for a red card.

VAR didn't feel compelled to intervene after checking the incident, though, which meant that the 22-year-old full-back avoided punishment altogether.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett hit out at Pawson, who had missed a simple caution.

"Reckless is when a player acts with a disregard for the danger to, or consequences for, an opponent and must be cautioned," he said.

"This, clearly, was a challenge that fulfilled the above criteria for a yellow card. In any game, whatever has gone on before, this was a challenge that needed to be acted on.

"VAR, of course, cannot be the lifebelt that comes to the rescue of Craig Pawson, and when he saw the Tarkowski challenge, he had to upgrade his yellow card.

"The referee should have been more decisive and pulled a yellow card out of his pocket!"

There is no doubt that Grealish was left in a lot of pain, and the calls for the game's second red card were completely understandable.

It was a high challenge, and with some force behind it. But fans were going to call for absolutely everything to get their team back onto a level playing field.

As commentators pointed out, though, the incident would have hurt a lot less had Grealish had properly-sized shin pads on.

It was evident just how tiny they were, and how very little of his shin they actually covered. It's understandable why players do it, but it opens them up to more injuries.

AC Milan’s shirt sponsor Emirates are set to make a change ahead of the 2027-28 season, according to a report.

As per Footy Headlines, the ‘Fly Better’ text will be removed from the shirts of Arsenal, Real Madrid and Milan ahead of next season. Instead, the airline will simply display the word ‘Emirates’ across the middle of the clubs that they sponsor.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is believed to be a record-breaking deal at least in Serie A, one that will net the club around €500m over the duration of the agreement. For many, it is a welcome return to a brand that became synonymous with Milan given the length of their last stint as the kit maker.

Newcastle United are likely among several European giants keeping tabs on Ethan Nwaneri's situation in the 2026-27 campaign.

The Arsenal gem is on loan at Borussia Dortmund this term, and he was expected to be the latest Englishman to shine in the Bundesliga.

It hasn't quite worked out for the 19-year-old, though, just a few months after his very disappointing six months at Marseille in 2025-26.

His same struggles are emerging at the Signal Iduna Park, and the Gunners are clearly becoming concerned by his lack of minutes.

According to the Daily Mail (24 November), the Premier League leaders are closely monitoring the situation ahead of the January transfer window.

Arsenal included a recall clause in Nwaneri's contract, a clause that was initially included in case an injury crisis emerged at the Emirates Stadium.

While Bukayo Saka's injury has left Mikel Arteta short in the final third, Nwaneri's lack of minutes is a far more pressing matter this season.

Nwaneri continues to prove himself in small bursts, and he could be the perfect addition to the Newcastle squad for the second half of the season.

#1908. Hansi Flick's blunt Real Madrid claim as Mourinho closes gap

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:38

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has insisted that he is not concerned by Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho, although his comments have taken on added significance after the Spanish capital club drew level on points with their bitter rivals.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, Flick dismissed questions about Madrid's improvement and emphasised that Barcelona were focused entirely on maintaining their position at the top of the table. At the time of his press conference on Saturday, the Catalan giants held a three-point advantage over Mourinho's side.

However, that lead disappeared later in the evening when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu. Carlos Espi's late winner lifted Los Blancos to 33 points, level with Barcelona, although Flick's team retain first place with a game in hand.

The sequence adds an intriguing dimension to Flick's remarks, made just hours before Madrid reduced the gap to zero. Barcelona now have an opportunity to restore their three-point advantage against Villarreal, but their manager's determination to ignore developments in the Spanish capital will be tested by an increasingly competitive title race.

Asked whether he had expected Real Madrid to improve so significantly under Mourinho, Flick declined to focus on the performances of Barcelona's biggest rivals.

"I don't care about Real Madrid. What they do is none of my business," the German said during his pre-match press conference, as reported by Brazilian outlet Trivela.

He explained that Barcelona's previous meeting with Madrid was already behind them and that his immediate priority was Sunday's home fixture against Villarreal.

"We are three points ahead of them and we want to maintain that position," Flick added. "That's what matters to us, not what Real Madrid are doing or how well they are playing."

Those comments were made before Madrid's victory over Celta and should not be interpreted as a response to Mourinho's latest result. Rather than criticising his Portuguese counterpart, Flick was attempting to shift attention towards Barcelona's own responsibilities in the title race.

The former Bayern Munich manager nevertheless acknowledged the improving standard of competition in La Liga, pointing to several teams capable of challenging the traditional dominance of Spain's two biggest clubs.

"There are also Atletico Madrid and Real Betis, who are having fantastic seasons. La Liga is very strong, that's the truth," he said when discussing Madrid's progress.

Flick was particularly complimentary about Villarreal, describing their head coach Inigo as an exceptional young manager with a promising future. His praise reflected the importance he attaches to Barcelona's next opponents, who could complicate the Catalans' efforts to maintain their advantage over Real Madrid.

While Flick was preparing his players for Villarreal, Mourinho's team faced a difficult evening against Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu.

The visitors made an excellent start, taking the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes. Madrid then missed an opportunity to equalise before half time when Kylian Mbappe failed to convert a penalty, leaving the hosts facing the prospect of a damaging defeat.

Jude Bellingham eventually restored parity in the 66th minute, finishing from inside the penalty area after Mbappe had provided the final pass. Madrid continued to push for a winner and were rewarded when Espi struck in the closing stages, converting the rebound after his initial header had been saved.

The victory was particularly significant in the context of the title race. Mourinho's side had begun the weekend three points behind Barcelona, but their determination to recover from an early setback ensured that the leaders would enter Sunday's fixture without any points advantage.

Madrid have now collected 33 points from 13 league matches, while Barcelona have the same total after 12 games. Flick's men therefore remain in control of their own position, although they will need to overcome Villarreal to re-establish a three-point cushion.

Barcelona were already preparing for a demanding encounter against opponents capable of causing problems for the leading sides, with Flick facing several selection decisions ahead of the fixture. The Catalans are looking to record their 12th league victory of the campaign and preserve their position at the summit.

Flick's refusal to dwell on Madrid's progress is consistent with his emphasis on Barcelona's own performances. Yet Saturday's result has removed their immediate margin for error, giving Sunday's meeting with Villarreal additional importance.

A victory would restore the three-point lead that Flick was referring to during his press conference. Anything less would leave Barcelona and Mourinho's Madrid separated by little or nothing at the top of La Liga heading into the next round of fixtures.

#1907. GdS: ‘Old to who?’ – Modric chasing Milan record while future remains unwritten

Luka Modric may be 41 years of age, but he shows no signs of slowing down. In fact, he remains crucial or both AC Milan and Croatia.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by pointing out that Sunday’s game will be a first for Modric, even given the hundreds of games he has played. The midfielder will face Frosinone for the first time, the 227th opponent of his long career (155 at club level and 72 for the national team).

In ten days, Modric will have gone from from London’s Wembley Stadium where he faced England, to the Opus Arena in Osijek, Croatia, where he beat the Czech Republic and played 90 minutes as captain, back to San Siro for the Frosinone game.

Yesterday, Luka returned to Milanello and trained with the Rossoneri, ready to take charge of the group again when the tournament resumes. He’s one of the eight players in the squad who have surpassed 800 minutes of total playing time across all competitions, including goalkeepers.

The Ballon d’Or winner has featured 13 times this season, with 11 being in the league (eight starts), and twice as a substitute in the Europa League. For his national team, he’s appeared in six Nations League matches, four of them from the start.

The match against Spain on October 6th was supposed to be his farewell to Croatia, but instead he was easily persuaded to stay and continue. He’s played 19 of the 21 matches since August, accumulating over a thousand minutes – 1,114 to be precise.

Modric scored for Milan at 40 years, five months and four days (the winner against Pisa) and is third in the ranking of the oldest goal scorers in the club’s history. Alessandro Costacurta is second (41 years, 25 days) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic is first (41 years, 5 months, and 15 days).

So, another record is in sight in the present, but what about the future? Modric is tied to Milan until the summer, with his contract expiring in June 2027. There are no further options for an extension but the relationship between player and club goes beyond written agreements.

Luka will decide his own future, as he did last summer, choosing to stay. He still wanted Milan despite being left behind without his family (who had since returned to Madrid) out of love for the Rossoneri. Next season, who knows?

#1906. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

#1905. Carlos Espi leads Europe's super-subs as Jose Mourinho explains role

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59

Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.

The Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start. No substitute across Europe's five major leagues has scored more this season when domestic and European competitions are combined.

His remarkable efficiency has become increasingly important to Mourinho, whose side needed another late rescue act after falling behind at the Santiago Bernabeu. Yet despite Espi's growing influence, the Portuguese manager believes the forward's particular qualities are better suited to certain situations than to Madrid's usual starting system.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised his young striker's attitude and penalty-box instincts, while acknowledging that his current role presents an unusual challenge for a player consistently delivering decisive contributions.

4️⃣ goles de Carlos Espí con Real Madrid que han significado el triunfo... ? ? @HBOMaxLat: https://t.co/JQG7BTvG44 #BenditaChampions | #TNTSportsEnHBOMax https://t.co/5wCmMv8agy

Madrid's victory against Celta offered another demonstration of why Espi has become such a valuable alternative to Kylian Mbappe.

The visitors took the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes, and Madrid's difficulties deepened when Mbappe fired a first-half penalty over the crossbar. Mourinho introduced Vinicius Junior after the interval, with the Brazilian helping transform the hosts' attacking performance.

Vinicius initiated the move that allowed Jude Bellingham to equalise in the 66th minute, combining with Mbappe before the England midfielder finished from inside the penalty area. With the game still level heading into the closing stages, Espi delivered the decisive contribution.

The youngster attacked a Vinicius cross in the 85th minute and saw his header saved by Ionut Radu, but reacted quickest to the rebound to put Madrid ahead.

It was his third winning goal in La Liga this season, following similarly decisive interventions against Espanyol in August and Elche in September. All three arrived after he had entered the pitch as a substitute, turning matches that were heading towards draws into victories.

Espi also scored during Madrid's dramatic 4-3 Champions League comeback against Roma in October, when Mourinho's side overturned a two-goal deficit in the closing minutes.

Those four goals have established the former Levante striker among Europe's most effective impact players, despite his limited opportunities. He has found the net with four of his six shots on target across those appearances, an extraordinary conversion rate that illustrates his ability to exploit the few chances he receives.

The £21m summer signing has already made a greater contribution than many might have anticipated when he arrived at the Bernabeu, particularly given the presence of Mbappe, Endrick and several other attacking options in Mourinho's squad.

His latest intervention also carried considerable significance in the title race. Madrid's victory moved them level with Barcelona on 33 points, although the Catalan club retained first place with a game in hand ahead of Sunday's encounter with Villarreal.

While Espi's scoring record could strengthen calls for a starting opportunity, Mourinho believes his effectiveness is closely connected to the circumstances in which he enters matches.

"Some players have specific characteristics," the Real Madrid coach explained after the Celta victory. "I don't want to say that Carlos won't start, or that Carlos can't play 90 minutes, because he can."

Mourinho pointed to the difference between Madrid's usual attacking approach and Espi's more traditional centre-forward profile. His team generally favour combination play and attacking runs into space, whereas the Spaniard thrives when opponents retreat towards their own penalty area.

"He's a guy with great quality in the box, a guy who's good in the air, a guy who plays well with his back to goal," Mourinho added, praising the striker's movement towards both posts.

The manager believes Espi becomes particularly dangerous when Madrid sustain pressure against opponents defending deep, allowing him to attack crosses and second balls inside crowded penalty areas.

That explains why Mourinho has repeatedly introduced him during the closing stages of difficult matches, often accepting a less balanced formation to increase his team's attacking presence.

The Portuguese coach also addressed the possibility of partnering Espi with Mbappe from the start, explaining that such an arrangement would require the wide players to take on greater defensive responsibilities. With Madrid's current attacking personnel, he does not believe a conventional 4-4-2 would provide the necessary balance.

? José Mourinho: “Carlos Espí is happy to be at Real Madrid. He knows he has the respect of his teammates, his coach, the fans”. “I will give him a start, 90 minutes, more game time… it will happen”. https://t.co/m02tx9LnFB

Nevertheless, Mourinho insisted that the forward's status is not permanent and expressed his desire to reward him with greater opportunities.

"Football history is full of players like him, and I believe he can be decisive without playing many minutes," he said.

The manager also praised Espi for accepting his role without demanding that Mbappe be dropped, describing a player who understands his position within the squad and is continuing to develop.

For his part, Espi appeared equally comfortable with that responsibility after Saturday's victory.

"I try to do what the manager asks of me. I'll make the most of every minute he gives me, and if I can help the team, even better," the striker told Real Madrid's official website.

With four goals already to his name and three league victories settled by his interventions, Espi has given Mourinho a compelling reason to consider him for a starting role.

However, the manager's explanation suggests that removing him from the bench would also mean sacrificing a specialist whose effectiveness has repeatedly rescued Madrid when their usual attacking approach has failed.

#1901. Tuttosport: Leadership and versatility – why Milan are targeting Man Utd’s Bruno Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes seems to be emerging as more and more of a concrete target for AC Milan in the coming months.

Owner Gerry Cardinale has already laid out the guidelines for the next transfer window (and future ones): he is fully committed to investing in strong players, regardless of age, with the aim of returning to competing for trophies.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan needd to bring in both talented young players who can shape the future squad, as well as players who can provide the backbone in terms of leadership and experience.

Milan are not only looking for players like Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi, therefore, but also those who can come into the dressing room and help younger players. The impact Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Simon Kjaer made on the last title-winning team is a good example of this.

Among the names on the shortlist, as reported by Tuttosport, is Bruno Fernandes. His contract with Manchester United is expiring at the end of the season, and the belief is that he could help fill the technical and experience void if Luka Modric departs.

Fernandes is an opportunity to be monitored closely, especially since the 32-year-old Portuguese would like to return to Italy, a country he has already frequented in his career given his experiences with Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria.

Bruno is negotiating a possible renewal with the Red Devils but the Manchester club want to propose a new contract with a lower salary than his current one (around €10-11m per season). There is a €65m release clause in his current contract, the paper adds.

This morning’s edition of the paper adds that the Portuguese star appeals because of his versatility, too. He can play as a deeper-lying midfield player – as he did under Ruben Amorim at Old Trafford – as a box-to-box player and as an attacking midfielder.

The latter is perhaps his preferred role, especially now that he is into his 30s. Interestingly, Amorim has switched from being locked into the 3-4-2-1 seen at United to now using more of a 4-2-3-1 in possession, so in theory there could be an ideal role waiting for Fernandes.

#1898. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

#1895. "Vini Jr is back": Spanish media hail Real Madrid star in Celta Vigo comeback victory

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 09:45

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior received glowing reviews from the Spanish media following his successful comeback against Celta Vigo on Saturday evening.

The Brazil international returned from a four-game La Liga suspension as Real Madrid overcame Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Bernabeu, although he was snubbed from the first whistle by Jose Mourinho.

The Blancos boss sided with Yan Diomande on the left-hand side, but with the score at 1-0 to Celta Vigo in the 57th minute, Mourinho introduced Vini Jr in place of right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold.

The 26-year-old helped to inspire a second-half Real Madrid comeback, as Jude Bellingham and Carlos Espi struck to extend the hosts' top-flight winning run to six matches and draw level on points with Barcelona at the top of the La Liga table.

Vinicius did not register a goal or assist on Saturday, but he made a driving run to claim a pre-assist for Bellingham's goal and delivered the cross that led to Espi's winner; the latter's first header was saved before he poked home the rebound.

In total, the attacker created two big chances, drew two fouls and made nine progressive carries during his 33-minute cameo, and his exploits were recognised by the press.

Eldesmarque awarded Vini Jr a 9/10, claiming that the South American 'redeemed himself' following his sending-off against Villarreal, while AS led with the headline 'Vinicius is back'.

Mundo Deportivo, meanwhile, stated that the Real Madrid winger is now showing 'signs of life' again, and his stellar cameo gives Blancos fans a 'glimmer of hope' that he can return to his former glories.

Relevo also described Vini Jr as 'revitalised' and hailed his burgeoning relationship with Espi, while Madrid-focused website La Galerna labelled him 'outstanding' and 'effervescent'.

Vinicius's eye-catching comeback performance has inevitably sparked debate about whether the attacker will be brought back into the starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

Vini Jr has started all four of Real Madrid's UCL games in 2026-27 so far, but he is yet to provide a goal or assist and has also failed to complete the full 90 in any of them.

Mourinho was asked about the prospect of Vinicius returning to the first XI in midweek, but the self-professed "bad boy" issued a spiky response to the question.

"I said yesterday, either from the bench or in the starting lineup. So you don't ask me the question on Monday and so you don't have so much to talk about for the next couple of days, I'm going to be a bad boy and end this story now. Starting Tuesday," Mourinho told reporters.

Vini Jr has provided just one goal and three assists in 13 Real Madrid appearances this season, and he has now gone seven games without scoring or setting up a teammate.
